A geofence is a boundary you draw on the map that raises an alert when something crosses it — so you can watch an area without staring at the screen.

Draft: written without screenshots. Add WinTAK geofence screenshots when available.

slides.title: What a geofence does
slides.html: A geofence monitors a shape on the map and notifies you when a tracked entity enters or exits it. Use it to watch an avenue of approach, a boundary, or a no-go area.

slides.title: Create a geofence
slides.html: Draw an area (circle or polygon) with the drawing tools, then turn it into a geofence from its options. The geofence is tied to that shape.

slides.title: Set the alert conditions
slides.html: Choose what triggers the alert — entering and/or exiting — and which entities to monitor (for example hostile or unknown tracks). Tune it so you get useful alerts, not noise.

slides.title: Receive alerts
slides.html: When the condition is met, WinTAK alerts you and highlights the crossing on the map. Acknowledge it, assess, and report through the RECON feed or your messaging tools as appropriate.
